labels.text: Create a cron schedule that runs in AGI cloud.
Manage the account's scheduled agent tasks in AGI cloud.
/schedule

S63.02.needs: a signed-in AGI account in the CLI
S63.02.note: The prompt is a single --prompt value; the code does not show how the saved prompt text is checked.
steps: In a terminal, type agi schedules create --name "Morning summary" --schedule "0 9 * * *" --prompt "Summarize my open pull requests."
Press Enter and read the printed result.
Type agi schedules list and find the new schedule.
Compare: a saved schedule appears with its name, its cron cadence, and the prompt you wrote is the one it runs.
S63.02.where: Terminal: agi schedules create --name "<name>" --schedule "0 9 * * *" --prompt "<prompt>". Or in an interactive agi session type /schedule and describe the routine.

labels.text: /save-routine

S63.03.needs: a finished task or chat turn in an interactive session, and a signed-in AGI account
S63.03.note: The slash command only asks the agent to create the routine; the saved result is confirmed by a later agi schedules list.
steps: Finish a task in an interactive agi session.
Type /save-routine 0 9 * * * and press Enter.
Wait for the reply, which says it will create a routine with cron_create.
Compare: one command turns the finished task into a saved routine, and the reply tells you the schedule and what each run will do.
S63.03.where: Interactive agi session: type /save-routine, optionally followed by a schedule such as 0 9 * * *, after the task is finished.

labels.text: Change a schedule's name, description, prompt, model, cron expression or time zone.
Optional description stored with the schedule.

S63.04.needs: a signed-in AGI account in the CLI
steps: Type agi schedules create --name "Weekly report" --schedule "0 9 * * 1" --prompt "Write the weekly report." --description "Runs every Monday".
Note the id printed in the result.
Type agi schedules edit <id> --name "Weekly status" --description "Monday status note".
Compare: the name and description both change, and the cadence and prompt stay the same.
S63.04.where: Terminal: agi schedules create --name "<name>" --description "<text>" and agi schedules edit <id> --name "<name>" --description "<text>".

labels.text: Change a schedule's name, description, prompt, model, cron expression or time zone.

S63.05.needs: a signed-in AGI account in the CLI
S63.05.note: The CLI has no multi-line editor (no $EDITOR use found); the prompt is one --prompt value, so a multi-line prompt has to be typed as a quoted string with line breaks.
steps: Type agi schedules edit <id> --prompt "Check the build and report failures."
Press Enter and read the printed result.
Type agi schedules list --json and find the prompt field of that schedule.
Compare: the new prompt is saved in place of the old one.
S63.05.where: Terminal: agi schedules edit <id> --prompt "<instructions>" (also set with --prompt on agi schedules create).

labels.text: 5-field cron expression, for example "0 9 * * *".
Run a schedule once now and wait for its result.

S63.12.needs: a signed-in AGI account; waiting for an occurrence to see it fire, or agi schedules run <id> to run now
S63.12.note: The CLI accepts only 5-field cron; daily, weekly or monthly picker presets are built by the web form, not the CLI (apps/cli/src/schedules.rs cron_create_request comment).
steps: Type agi schedules create --name "Daily" --schedule "0 9 * * *" --prompt "Say good morning."
Note the id in the result.
Type agi schedules list and read the cadence shown for it.
Compare: the schedule shows the cron cadence and a next run time, and it fires on each occurrence.
S63.12.where: Terminal: agi schedules create --schedule "<5-field cron>", for example "0 9 * * *" for every day at 09:00.

labels.text: IANA time zone the cron expression is read in. Defaults to this machine's.

S63.13.needs: none beyond a signed-in AGI account
steps: Type agi schedules create --name "Lunch" --schedule "0 12 * * *" --prompt "Lunch reminder." --timezone "America/New_York".
Read the result line; it shows the time zone after the cadence.
Type agi schedules edit <id> --timezone "Europe/London" and read the result.
Compare: the zone shown changes to the one you set, and the next run time is calculated in that zone.
S63.13.where: Terminal: agi schedules create --timezone "<IANA zone>" or agi schedules edit <id> --timezone "<IANA zone>".

S63.14.note: Only 5-field cron is accepted by agi schedules create and edit; I searched apps/cli for interval, iCalendar, RRULE and run-window options and found none. The CLI only displays server-sent interval and once schedule types (schedules.rs schedule_cadence).

labels.text: Run a schedule's task whenever an event arrives from GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar or a connector.
`agi --daemon` runs it.

S63.15.needs: an outside account (GitHub, Slack, Gmail or Google Calendar) connected to AGI for the chosen source; for the webhook, a running agi --daemon
S63.15.note: The schedule-trigger sources in the CLI do not list webhook; the webhook path is the top-level agi triggers command, which runs only under the daemon. Whether the hosted service fires the trigger was not verified from the CLI code.
steps: Type agi schedules triggers add <schedule> --source github --account owner/name --event pull_request.opened
Read the printed trigger; it shows the trigger id and its endpoint.
Open a new pull request on that repository (or send the event).
Compare: the schedule starts a run when the event arrives, and agi schedules runs <schedule> shows a run with a trigger source.
S63.15.where: Terminal: agi schedules triggers add <schedule> --source github|slack|gmail|google_calendar|connector. Webhook: agi triggers add <id> --webhook <path> --prompt "<prompt>", with agi --daemon running.

labels.text: Only fire when this holds, written FIELD OPERATOR VALUE, such as "data.baseRef equals main". Repeatable; all must hold.
Ignore repeats for this many seconds after a run starts (0 turns it off).

S63.16.needs: an outside account connected for the chosen source
S63.16.note: The daemon filter quiet period is enforced in apps/cli/src/daemon.rs (quiet_period_secs); the schedule-trigger debounce is sent to the hosted service and not checked in the CLI code.
steps: Type agi schedules triggers add <schedule> --source github --account owner/name --event pull_request.opened --when "data.baseRef equals main" --debounce 60
Read the printed trigger and check the event and condition are shown.
Open a pull request into a different branch, then one into main.
Compare: only the matching event starts a run, and repeats inside the debounce window do not start another.
S63.16.where: Terminal: agi schedules triggers add <schedule> --source github --event <type> --when "<FIELD OPERATOR VALUE>" --debounce <seconds>. Daemon triggers: agi triggers filter <id> --event <type> --when "/json/pointer=value" --quiet-for <seconds>.

labels.text: List the account's schedules with status, cadence and next run.

S63.20.needs: a signed-in AGI account with at least one schedule
steps: Create a schedule with agi schedules create (see S63.02).
Type agi schedules list.
Read the line under each schedule's name.
Compare: the line shows next: with the next run time, or next: not scheduled when none is set.

labels.text: last error:
List the account's schedules with status, cadence and next run.

S63.21.needs: a signed-in AGI account with a schedule that has run
S63.21.note: The line reads last: never until the schedule has run.
steps: Run agi schedules run <id> to run a schedule now.
Type agi schedules list.
Read the last: value and any last error: line under that schedule.
Compare: the last run time shows, and a failed last run shows its error line.
S63.21.where: Terminal: agi schedules list (last: field), and agi schedules runs <id> for run results.

labels.text: Show a schedule's run history.
This schedule has not run yet.

S63.22.needs: a schedule that has run at least once
S63.22.note: The code does not set the order of runs; it prints what the server returns.
steps: Type agi schedules runs <id>.
Read each run line: its id, status, trigger source, start time and duration.
Type agi schedules runs <id> --limit 5 to see fewer runs.
Compare: past runs are listed with status and time, newest first as the server returns them.

labels.text: output:
Show a schedule's run history.

S63.23.needs: a schedule whose run produced output
steps: Type agi schedules runs <id>.
Find an output: line under a run.
Type agi schedules runs <id> --json for the full output.
Compare: each run shows its output text, not only its status. Long output is cut after a few lines, and --json has the full text.
S63.23.where: Terminal: agi schedules runs <id> (output: lines under each run); agi schedules run <id> for a run started now.

labels.text: Stop a schedule from firing until it is resumed.
Let a paused schedule fire again.

S63.24.needs: a signed-in AGI account with a schedule
steps: Type agi schedules pause <id> and read the result.
Type agi schedules list and check the status shown for that schedule.
Type agi schedules resume <id>.
Compare: the schedule stops firing while paused, is kept in the list, and fires again after resume.
S63.24.where: Terminal: agi schedules pause <id> and agi schedules resume <id>

labels.text: Delete a schedule by id or name.

S63.27.needs: a schedule you can delete; a test schedule is recommended because deletion cannot be undone
S63.27.note: The confirmation text says the run history goes with it and cannot be undone.
steps: Type agi schedules delete <id>.
At the confirmation, read the warning, then answer no and check the schedule is still in agi schedules list.
Type agi schedules delete <id> again and answer yes.
Compare: after the confirmation the schedule is gone from agi schedules list, and it no longer fires.

labels.text: Approve the step a paused run is waiting on, and let the run continue.
paused: a run needed your approval

S63.32.needs: a schedule whose unattended run is waiting for approval, which the tester may not be able to cause from the CLI
S63.32.note: The CLI only shows and resolves the pause; the pause itself is set by the hosted run (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts), which the CLI code does not show.
steps: Type agi schedules list and find a schedule showing paused: a run needed your approval.
Type agi schedules runs <id> and read the waiting for your approval block with its actions.
Type agi schedules approve <id> and answer the prompt (or add --yes).
Compare: the run continues after approval, and its status changes from awaiting_approval.
S63.32.where: Terminal: agi schedules runs <id> (shows the waiting approval), then agi schedules approve <id> or agi schedules deny <id>

labels.text: ran late for the occurrence due

S63.33.needs: a schedule that missed an occurrence, which is hard to cause from the CLI
S63.33.note: The CLI prints a missed-run line only for runs that ran late; it prints no reason for a skipped occurrence, so Expected is only partly met from the code.
steps: Type agi schedules runs <id>.
Look for a line ran late for the occurrence due <time> under a run.
Type agi schedules runs <id> --json and look for missedExecution and skipped.
Compare: a late run says it ran late for its due time. A skipped occurrence shows only its status, with no reason printed by the CLI.
